title: 100 Reel Ideas
subtitle: Short-form content that makes people feel seen, gives them a tiny win, and invites them in.

howToUse.label: Posting mix
howToUse.text: Roughly 3 Seen : 2 Helped : 1 Belong each week. Seen reels grow reach, Helped reels earn saves, Belong reels convert followers into session attendees.

howToUse.label: Hook rule
howToUse.text: The first line is on screen within 1.5 seconds. In Pillar 1, never say 'ADHD' in the hook; describe the moment instead. The word can appear in the caption.

howToUse.label: Help rule
howToUse.text: In Pillar 2, the viewer must be able to complete the win without leaving the app. The CTA is 'save this', not 'download'.

howToUse.label: Consent rule
howToUse.text: Pillar 3 uses real members only with written permission; blur or crop session grids otherwise.

howToUse.label: CTA ladder
howToUse.text: Seen → comment 'me'. Helped → save. Belong → link in bio to tomorrow's session. Keep one CTA per reel.

howToUse.label: Series it
howToUse.text: Recurring formats (e.g. 'Why you...' on Mondays, 'Start button' on Wednesdays, 'Tomorrow, 9am' as the standard end card) train the audience to come back.

starterSequence: Week 4: repeat the two best performers in a new format, and post #98 (why we don't do streaks).

pillars.name: Seen
pillars.blurb: Storytelling that names the experience. Goal: recognition and shares.

ideas.title: Why you clean the whole kitchen instead of sending one email
ideas.description: Split screen: spotless kitchen vs. an untouched email draft. VO: the email isn't hard, it's undefined. Your brain picks the task with a clear finish line.

ideas.title: You're not lazy. You're waiting for the task to feel possible.
ideas.description: Talking head describing task paralysis as a wall you can see through but can't walk through. Not a choice, a wall.

ideas.title: The 3 hours before an appointment where you can't do anything else
ideas.description: POV skit: clock ticking, person frozen on the couch, 'I'll just wait.' Names 'waiting mode' without naming anything clinical.

ideas.title: When 'just reply to one text' becomes a 9-day project
ideas.description: WhatsApp unread counter climbs day by day. The guilt makes the reply heavier, which makes it later, which makes the guilt heavier.

ideas.title: Why you do your best work at 11pm the night before
ideas.description: The deadline lends you the urgency your brain can't generate on its own. Borrowed fuel, not bad character.

ideas.title: You have 47 tabs open because closing one feels like losing it
ideas.description: Slow pan across a browser full of tabs. If it's out of sight, it's gone. Tabs are your external memory.

ideas.title: The 'I'll start after this video' loop
ideas.description: Autoplay screen recording, clock in the corner jumping 10 min, 30 min, 1 hr. End card: 'Sound familiar?'

ideas.title: Why you can play a game for 6 hours but can't do taxes for 6 minutes
ideas.description: Interest runs your engine, importance doesn't. Explains the interest-based attention idea in plain words.

ideas.title: Buying a new planner is the most productive you'll feel all month
ideas.description: Pan across a shelf of barely-used planners. Newness feels like progress; it wears off by week two.

ideas.title: When someone says 'just make a to-do list'
ideas.description: Reaction skit: unroll a list of 43 items, all marked urgent. The list isn't the problem, choosing is.

ideas.title: The shower argument you win every single time
ideas.description: Creator rehearsing a conversation in the shower. The mind runs its own playlist, all day.

ideas.title: You didn't forget their birthday. You remembered it at 2am, three days early, and never again.
ideas.description: Text-on-screen timeline of the thought appearing once and vanishing. Memory that doesn't hold on to things you care about.

ideas.title: Why a 5-minute task sits on your list for 5 weeks
ideas.description: Small tasks have no urgency, so they never win the fight for attention. They just quietly pile up.

ideas.title: The chair pile isn't mess. It's a to-do list you can see.
ideas.description: Close-up of the clothes chair. Reframe: you keep things visible because hidden things stop existing.

ideas.title: Leaving the house: keys, phone, wallet, back for keys, back for charger
ideas.description: Door-exit skit looped four times, each time returning for one more thing.

ideas.title: You're 20 minutes early or 20 minutes late. Never on time.
ideas.description: Two-panel skit. Time doesn't feel like a line; it's 'now' and 'not now'.

ideas.title: When your manager says 'quick call?' and your body goes cold
ideas.description: Slack notification, heart-rate rising text, spiralling thoughts. Names the dread of assumed criticism.

ideas.title: Why you start five new hobbies every year
ideas.description: Montage of guitar, pottery, coding, running shoes. Not flaky: your brain loves the learning curve.

ideas.title: The dishes aren't the problem. Starting the dishes is the problem.
ideas.description: Static shot of a sink; creator stares for 20 seconds, then text: 'the hardest part is the first plate.'

ideas.title: You rehearse the phone call 11 times and still don't make it
ideas.description: Tally marks on a notepad for each rehearsal. Phone stays face-down.

ideas.title: Sunday, 7pm: the dread arrives on schedule
ideas.description: Clock hits 7, lighting goes dim, the whole week lands at once as one blob.

ideas.title: Your brain in a Monday stand-up
ideas.description: Inner monologue captions: listening, listening, lunch thoughts, 'sorry, can you repeat that?'

ideas.title: Being told you have 'so much potential' for 20 years
ideas.description: Quiet talking head. How a compliment turns into a weight. Emotional, no fixes offered.

ideas.title: Why you're exhausted after doing 'nothing' all day
ideas.description: Avoiding a task takes effort. Fighting yourself for 8 hours burns more energy than doing the thing.

ideas.title: The gym membership, the gym clothes, and a gym that has never seen you
ideas.description: Light comedy flat-lay of new gear with tags still on. Ends kind, not mocking.

ideas.title: When you finally sit down to work and suddenly need water, a snack, a playlist and a clean desk
ideas.description: Speed-ramped setup spiral. 40 minutes later, still no work.

ideas.title: Why you can't watch a movie without your phone
ideas.description: Too little stimulation feels uncomfortable, so the brain adds a second screen. Not rudeness.

ideas.title: You're not bad with money. You're bad with boring admin that costs money.
ideas.description: Stack of late fees, forgotten subscriptions, unclaimed refunds. The hidden tax of 'I'll do it later'.

ideas.title: Diwali cleaning: you found your 2019 notebook and read it for two hours
ideas.description: India-specific skit. Cleaning becomes a side quest; the room stays half-done.

ideas.title: When a task has 3 steps and you can't see step 1
ideas.description: 'Plan the trip' shown as a fogged-out screen. The first action is invisible, so nothing starts.

ideas.title: The guilt of resting when you haven't 'earned' it, and you never feel like you've earned it
ideas.description: Couch shot, captions of the inner critic. Gentle ending line: rest isn't a reward.

ideas.title: Why you over-promise on Monday and disappear by Thursday
ideas.description: Monday-you signs up for everything; Thursday-you inherits the bill. Optimism about your future self.

ideas.title: You'll hit anyone else's deadline and none of your own
ideas.description: Split screen: boss's task done in an hour; personal project untouched for a year. Outside pressure works.

ideas.title: When the task matters so much you can't touch it
ideas.description: The job application that's been 'almost ready' for three weeks. Importance turns into paralysis.

ideas.title: Unread emails: 4,382. Anxiety: yes.
ideas.description: Inbox zoom-in, heartbeat sound design. Ends with 'you're not the only one.'

ideas.title: Why the 30 minutes between tasks wreck your day
ideas.description: Switching gears costs more than the task itself. The 'in-between' where nothing happens.

ideas.title: You remember every friend's problems and forget your own dentist appointment
ideas.description: Warm skit. Caring is easy; remembering your own admin isn't.

ideas.title: 'Padhai mein dhyan do' / 'just be more disciplined'
ideas.description: Hinglish skit with a parent. Validates the kid who was trying the whole time.

ideas.title: When your brain finally switches on, and you have 40 minutes before it switches off
ideas.description: Lights-on moment, frantic typing, then fade. Names the unpredictable focus window.

ideas.title: It's not that you don't care. It's that caring doesn't turn into doing.
ideas.description: Signature closer. Slow talking head, one line, long pause. Series anchor for the pillar.

pillars.name: Helped
pillars.blurb: Free, instant, tiny help. Goal: a felt win and saves.

ideas.title: Can't start? Do the first 2 minutes with me. Timer starts now.
ideas.description: On-screen 2:00 countdown; creator starts their own task alongside. The reel itself is the tool.

ideas.title: Brain dump in 60 seconds
ideas.description: Write everything in your head. Circle three. Ignore the rest for today. Creator does it live on paper.

ideas.title: The ugly first draft trick
ideas.description: Write the email badly on purpose. Show a terrible draft becoming a decent one in 30 seconds.

ideas.title: Make step one so small it's embarrassing
ideas.description: 'Open laptop' is a valid step one. Show a real task broken into ridiculous micro-steps.

ideas.title: Stuck? Say the next physical action out loud
ideas.description: 'Work on report' becomes 'open the doc called Report'. Verbs your hands can do.

ideas.title: The launch pad: one spot by the door
ideas.description: Tray for keys, wallet, phone, earphones. Set it up in 20 seconds on camera.

ideas.title: Five minutes, then you're allowed to stop
ideas.description: Permission to quit lowers the wall to start. Most people keep going.

ideas.title: Pair the boring task with a treat
ideas.description: That podcast only plays while you do dishes. Show the rule in action.

ideas.title: Double your time estimate. Then add 10 minutes.
ideas.description: Walk through one real estimate: 'shower 10 min' is actually 25. Plan with the real number.

ideas.title: Name your alarms with the consequence
ideas.description: 'LEAVE NOW or you miss the metro' beats a silent 8:15. Screen-record setting one up.

ideas.title: Under two minutes? Do it while this reel plays
ideas.description: Countdown overlay; viewer clears one tiny thing before the reel loops.

ideas.title: Work with me for 60 seconds
ideas.description: Phone propped on a desk, creator working silently, ambient sound, timer. The smallest body double.

ideas.title: Tomorrow's first task on a sticky note, tonight
ideas.description: Stick it on your laptop lid. Morning-you doesn't have to decide anything.

ideas.title: Make time visible
ideas.description: Analog clock or a visual timer on the desk. Time you can see is time you can feel.

ideas.title: Overwhelmed? Sort into today / this week / someday
ideas.description: 45-second live sort of a messy list. Most items land in 'someday', and that's the relief.

ideas.title: Can't pick what's first? Choose what makes tomorrow easiest
ideas.description: A single decision rule for when everything feels equal.

ideas.title: The Reset 10
ideas.description: Ten-minute timer, one room, go. Speed-ramped before/after.

ideas.title: Put the thing you'll forget where you'll trip over it
ideas.description: Bill on the kettle, parcel on the doormat, charger on the pillow. Visibility beats memory.

ideas.title: One text for instant accountability
ideas.description: 'Starting X now, check on me at 4.' Show sending it to a friend.

ideas.title: 60-second reset when everything feels like too much
ideas.description: Guided breath: breathe out longer than you breathe in. Creator does it with the viewer.

ideas.title: Stalled? Change chairs.
ideas.description: New spot, new start. Show someone move from bed to kitchen table and begin.

ideas.title: Tonight, write a done list instead of a to-do list
ideas.description: Evidence you did things. Creator writes theirs on camera, including the tiny ones.

ideas.title: Leave a breadcrumb when you stop
ideas.description: Sticky note: 'next I was going to...'. Future-you restarts in seconds.

ideas.title: The three-alarm morning
ideas.description: Wake. Move. Leave. Three labelled alarms, nothing else to decide.

ideas.title: Pick one 'we're starting' song
ideas.description: Headphones on, same song every time. A ritual your brain learns as the start signal.

ideas.title: Turn the task into verbs
ideas.description: 'Plan the trip' becomes five verbs: check dates, message group, compare trains, book, share. Tap-along text.

ideas.title: Unsubscribe from five emails while I count
ideas.description: Countdown do-along. Tiny, visible win in under a minute.

ideas.title: Decide what 'done' looks like before you start
ideas.description: The good-enough line stops a 20-minute task becoming a 3-hour polish.

ideas.title: Phone in another room for 25 minutes. That's the reel.
ideas.description: Creator walks the phone away; text-only reel with a 25-minute suggestion.

ideas.title: Stop mid-sentence when you end work
ideas.description: Tomorrow's start becomes obvious. Show the half-sentence left on screen.

ideas.title: Brain too loud to sleep? Two-minute worry park
ideas.description: Dump every loop on paper, close the notebook, lights off.

ideas.title: Batch the boring
ideas.description: All calls on Tuesday at 11. One block, one dread, then done.

ideas.title: Save this reel. It's your start button.
ideas.description: A 60-second countdown with a calm voice: 'pick one thing, we're starting.' Built to be replayed.

ideas.title: The 5-4-3-2-1 stand-up
ideas.description: Count down out loud and stand before your brain argues. Demo from couch to desk.

ideas.title: Comment the one thing you're avoiding. Then go do two minutes of it.
ideas.description: Engagement reel that doubles as accountability. Creator replies to comments the next day.

pillars.name: Belong
pillars.blurb: Human connection with zero performance pressure. Goal: first session, then return.

ideas.title: 9am. 40 strangers. Cameras optional. Everyone just starts.
ideas.description: Timelapse of a live Done Together session grid. No talking, just work.

ideas.title: Nobody checks your work here
ideas.description: You say what you'll do, then you do it. That's the whole deal. Host voiceover over session footage.

ideas.title: I didn't finish my task. Nobody cared. I came back the next day.
ideas.description: Member story (with consent). The point is returning, not completing.

ideas.title: What a body doubling session actually looks like
ideas.description: Walkthrough: join, one-line intro, mics off, timer, quick share at the end.

ideas.title: 'I filed my taxes in a room full of people I've never met'
ideas.description: Member testimonial. The task they avoided for months, done in 50 minutes with company.

ideas.title: Your only job: show up. Not be productive. Show up.
ideas.description: Short manifesto-style reel. Sets the zero-pressure promise.

ideas.title: The 30-second check-in
ideas.description: Say one thing you're working on. That's it. Montage of quick, low-stakes intros.

ideas.title: Missed a week? Welcome back. No streak. No shame.
ideas.description: Directly speaks to the comeback moment. Warm host greeting.

ideas.title: Why working next to strangers works when working alone doesn't
ideas.description: Simple science: other people's presence nudges your brain into gear. No jargon.

ideas.title: POV: your first body doubling session
ideas.description: Nervous join, expecting judgment. Everyone is just quietly working. Relief.

ideas.title: Meet the 9am regulars
ideas.description: Mini-profiles: 'I'm Riya, I show up to write.' Identity, not performance.

ideas.title: 'I wrote two lines.'
ideas.description: End-of-session chat where tiny wins get celebrated like big ones.

ideas.title: The 11pm night-owl crew
ideas.description: A session for people whose brains switch on late. Your rhythm is welcome.

ideas.title: What people worked on today
ideas.description: Scrolling anonymised list: 'cleaned one drawer', 'answered 3 emails', 'finally booked the doctor'. Small is normal.

ideas.title: You don't have to talk
ideas.description: Some days, camera off and just being there is the win.

ideas.title: Host confession: I didn't want to start today either
ideas.description: The host is human too. Shared struggle lowers the bar to join.

ideas.title: Work with me for 25 minutes
ideas.description: Full-length ambient co-working reel with timer. Replayable body double for anyone, anytime.

ideas.title: 'Why do you need strangers to do the dishes?'
ideas.description: Answering a partner or parent's question kindly. Useful for proxy audiences too.

ideas.title: Day 1 camera off. Day 12 said hi. Day 30 hosting.
ideas.description: One member's journey told in three frames. Belonging grows slowly.

ideas.title: The 'I showed up' wall
ideas.description: Collage of first names / avatars (with consent) who attended this week. Showing up is the achievement.

ideas.title: Exam season study-along
ideas.description: CA, UPSC, board exam students studying together. India-specific session promo.

ideas.title: Friday wind-down: close loops together
ideas.description: No new tasks. Just finish small things with others before the weekend.

ideas.title: Why we don't do streaks
ideas.description: Founder talking head on the brand philosophy: coming back after a gap should feel good, not guilty.

ideas.title: Tag the friend who also 'can't start'
ideas.description: Bring a buddy. Two people who struggle, starting together.

ideas.title: Tomorrow, 9am. Bring whatever you're avoiding.
ideas.description: Standing invitation. Use as the recurring end card for the whole series.
